subtopics.name: Chemical Properties of Aldehydes and Ketones

questions.stem: Which of the following on treatment with $\mathrm{H_2O_2}$ in presence of $\mathrm{NaOH}$ followed by acid hydrolysis gives $o$-hydroxybenzaldehyde (salicylaldehyde) via Baeyer-Villiger type oxidation?
questions.solution: Treatment of $o$-hydroxyacetophenone with alkaline $\mathrm{H_2O_2}$ (Dakin reaction, a variation of Baeyer-Villiger oxidation) yields catechol (or salicylaldehyde under controlled oxidation/hydrolysis conditions). Specifically, the migration of the aryl group with the $o$-OH substituent occurs, which upon hydrolysis yields the corresponding phenol/aldehyde derivative.

questions.stem: Which of the following compounds does not give iodoform test?
questions.solution: The iodoform test is given by compounds containing a methyl ketone group ($\mathrm{CH_3-CO-}$) or a methyl carbinol group ($\mathrm{CH_3-CH(OH)-}$). Pentan-3-one ($\mathrm{CH_3-CH_2-CO-CH_2-CH_3}$) does not contain either of these groups, so it does not give the iodoform test.

questions.stem: An organic compound 'A' on treatment with $\mathrm{O}_3$ followed by $\mathrm{Zn/H}_2\mathrm{O}$ gives formaldehye and 2-methylpropanal. Compound 'A' is:
questions.solution:
The reductive ozonolysis products are formaldehyde ($\mathrm{HCHO}$) and 2-methylpropanal (($\mathrm{CH}_3)_2\mathrm{CH-CHO}$).
To find compound 'A', join the carbonyl carbons with a double bond:
$(\mathrm{CH}_3)_2\mathrm{CH-CH}=\mathrm{CH}_2$
This is 3-methylbut-1-ene.

questions.stem: The number of stereocenters present in the product obtained by the reaction of benzaldehyde with $\mathrm{HCN}$ is _________.
questions.solution:
Reaction of benzaldehyde ($\mathrm{C_6H_5CHO}$) with $\mathrm{HCN}$ yields benzaldehyde cyanohydrin:
$\mathrm{C_6H_5-CH(OH)-CN}$.
The central carbon is bonded to four different groups: $-\mathrm{H}$, $-\mathrm{OH}$, $-\mathrm{CN}$, and $-\mathrm{C_6H_5}$.
Therefore, it has 1 stereocenter.

questions.stem: The reaction of benzaldehyde with concentrated $\mathrm{NaOH}$ solution gives benzyl alcohol and sodium benzoate. This reaction is known as:
questions.solution: Aldehydes having no $\alpha$-hydrogen atoms (like benzaldehyde) undergo self-oxidation and reduction (disproportionation) on treatment with concentrated alkali to produce alcohol and salt of carboxylic acid. This is the Cannizzaro reaction.

questions.stem: The total number of stereoisomers obtained when 3-methylhex-2-ene reacts with $\mathrm{HBr}$ in the presence of peroxide is _________.
questions.solution:
Addition of $\mathrm{HBr}$ in presence of peroxide to 3-methylhex-2-ene ($\mathrm{CH_3-CH=C(CH_3)-CH_2-CH_2-CH_3}$) occurs via anti-Markovnikov pathway.
$\mathrm{Br}$ attaches to C2 and $\mathrm{H}$ to C3.
Product is 2-bromo-3-methylhexane: $\mathrm{CH_3-CH(Br)-CH(CH_3)-CH_2-CH_2-CH_3}$.
This molecule has 2 chiral centers (C2 and C3) and is unsymmetrical.
Number of stereoisomers $= 2^n = 2^2 = 4$.

questions.stem: Which of the following will not give the iodoform test?
questions.solution: The iodoform test is given by compounds having a $\mathrm{CH_3-CO-}$ group or a $\mathrm{CH_3-CH(OH)-}$ group. Benzophenone ($\mathrm{C_6H_5-CO-C_6H_5}$) does not contain a methyl ketone group, so it does not give the iodoform test.

questions.stem: Benzaldehyde on reaction with concentrated $\mathrm{NaOH}$ solution followed by acidification yields:
questions.solution: Benzaldehyde does not contain any $\alpha$-hydrogen. On heating with concentrated alkali, it undergoes Cannizzaro reaction (self-redox) to produce benzyl alcohol (reduction product) and sodium benzoate (oxidation product). After acidification, benzoic acid is formed from sodium benzoate.

questions.stem: Which of the following compounds will not give Fehling's test?
questions.solution: Fehling's solution oxidizes aliphatic aldehydes but does not oxidize aromatic aldehydes like benzaldehyde because aromatic aldehydes are less reactive and lack $\alpha$-hydrogens participating in the tautomeric enol form required for reduction of the complexed $\mathrm{Cu^{2+}}$ in alkaline media.

questions.stem:
How many of the following compounds give a positive Fehling's test?
- Glucose
- Fructose
- Sucrose
- Benzaldehyde
- Acetaldehyde
- Acetone
questions.solution:
- Glucose (reducing sugar): Positive
- Fructose (reducing ketose, isomerizes to aldose under basic conditions): Positive
- Sucrose (non-reducing sugar): Negative
- Benzaldehyde (aromatic aldehyde, does not reduce Fehling's solution): Negative
- Acetaldehyde (aliphatic aldehyde): Positive
- Acetone (ketone): Negative
Total positive tests = 3.

questions.stem: When benzaldehyde is treated with concentrated $\text{NaOH}$ solution, it undergoes Cannizzaro reaction. The products formed are :
questions.solution: Benzaldehyde contains no $\alpha$-hydrogens and undergoes self-oxidation and reduction (disproportionation) in the presence of strong concentrated alkali (Cannizzaro reaction) to form sodium benzoate and benzyl alcohol.

questions.stem: Benzaldehyde on reaction with concentrated $\mathrm{NaOH}$ solution gives Benzyl alcohol and Sodium benzoate. This reaction is known as:
questions.solution: Aldehydes with no $\alpha$-hydrogen atoms, such as benzaldehyde, undergo self-oxidation and reduction (disproportionation) on treatment with concentrated alkali to yield alcohol and salt of carboxylic acid. This is the Cannizzaro reaction.

questions.stem: A ketones $A$ ($C_4H_8O$) on reaction with $CH_3MgBr$ followed by hydrolysis gives an alcohol $B$. Compound $B$ on heating with concentrated $H_2SO_4$ gives a major product $C$. The total number of double bond isomers (including stereoisomers) possible for $C$ is _____.
questions.solution:
Ketone $A$ must be 2-butanone ($CH_3COCH_2CH_3$).
Reaction with $CH_3MgBr$ followed by hydrolysis gives 2-methylbutan-2-ol ($CH_3-C(OH)(CH_3)-CH_2-CH_3$).
Dehydration of 2-methylbutan-2-ol gives 2-methylbut-2-ene (major, more substituted) and 2-methylbut-1-ene (minor).
For major product $C$ (2-methylbut-2-ene), there are no geometrical isomers (one double-bonded carbon has two identical methyl groups).
Thus, the number of stereoisomers for $C$ is just $1$.

questions.stem: Cannizzaro reaction is not given by:
questions.solution: The Cannizzaro reaction is given by aldehydes which do not have an $\alpha$-hydrogen atom. Formaldehyde, benzaldehyde, and trimethylacetaldehyde lack $\alpha$-hydrogens. Acetaldehyde ($CH_3CHO$) contains three $\alpha$-hydrogens and undergoes aldol condensation instead.

questions.stem: Which of the following compounds will give a positive Fehling's test?
questions.solution: Fehling's solution is a mild oxidizing agent that oxidizes aliphatic aldehydes (like acetaldehyde) but does not oxidize aromatic aldehydes (like benzaldehyde) or ketones.

questions.stem: Which of the following compounds will not give a yellow precipitate with iodine and sodium hydroxide?
questions.solution: The iodoform test (treatment with $\text{I}_2/\text{NaOH}$) is positive for compounds containing a $\text{CH}_3\text{CO}-$ group or a $\text{CH}_3\text{CH(OH)}-$ group. Pentan-2-one, ethanol (oxidized to acetaldehyde), and acetophenone contain these units and give a yellow precipitate of $\text{CHI}_3$. Pentanoic acid does not undergo the iodoform reaction.

questions.stem: The reaction of benzaldehyde with concentrated $\mathrm{NaOH}$ solution followed by acid hydrolysis gives:
questions.solution: Benzaldehyde does not contain any $\alpha$-hydrogen atom. Therefore, when treated with concentrated alkali ($\mathrm{NaOH}$), it undergoes Cannizzaro reaction (disproportionation) to yield benzyl alcohol (reduced product) and sodium benzoate (oxidized product). Acidification of sodium benzoate would yield benzoic acid along with benzyl alcohol.

questions.stem: The reaction of benzaldehyde with concentrated $\mathrm{NaOH}$ solution gives benzyl alcohol and sodium benzoate. This reaction is known as:
questions.solution: Benzaldehyde does not contain any $\alpha$-hydrogen. In the presence of concentrated alkali, it undergoes self-oxidation and reduction (disproportionation) to yield benzyl alcohol and sodium benzoate. This is the Cannizzaro reaction.

questions.stem: The reaction of benzaldehyde with concentrated $\mathrm{NaOH}$ solution gives a mixture of benzaldehyde's reduction and oxidation products. This reaction is known as:
questions.solution: Aldehydes lacking $\alpha$-hydrogen atoms (such as benzaldehyde, $\mathrm{C_6H_5CHO}$) undergo self-oxidation and reduction (disproportionation) on treatment with concentrated alkali to yield alcohol (benzyl alcohol) and the salt of the carboxylic acid (sodium benzoate). This is the Cannizzaro reaction.

questions.stem: Which of the following compounds will not give a yellow precipitate of iodoform when treated with iodine and sodium hydroxide?
questions.solution: The iodoform test is given by compounds containing the $\mathrm{CH_3CO-}$ group or $\mathrm{CH_3CH(OH)-}$ group. Pentan-3-one ($\mathrm{CH_3CH_2-CO-CH_2CH_3}$) lacks a methyl carbonyl group, so it does not give the iodoform test.
